bullets.point: Banking sector buffers: IMF staff find the banking system sound, with an aggregate Tier 1 regulatory capital ratio above 20 percent and a liquidity coverage ratio of 175 percent at end-2025, well above regulatory minima.

Too-big-to-fail reforms: Staff urge implementing TBTF reforms requiring G-SIBs to fully cover foreign subsidiaries with CET1 capital—adding US$20 billion for UBS. Authorities agree foreign subsidiaries should be fully backed with CET1 capital.

Real estate vulnerabilities: Staff urge adding DSTI limits as apartment prices exceed fundamentals by 15–40 percent. Authorities consider current settings appropriate, though staff note property-related loans comprise 86 percent of bank lending.

Liquidity and nonbank supervision: The SNB will launch an Extended Liquidity Facility in 2027, while staff recommend a public liquidity backstop. Nonbank risks remain contained, though insurers hold 37 percent of assets in real estate.

External downside risks: High-likelihood geopolitical tensions and potential US tariffs up to 12.5 percent carry medium/high impact. Under a severe scenario, GDP growth falls by 0.9 percentage points over two years; staff advise letting automatic stabilizers operate.

Disinflationary risk response: Headline inflation reached 0.5 percent in June 2026. Facing high-likelihood disinflation risks (high impact), staff advocate readying negative rates and FX intervention. Authorities view FX interventions as flexible standalone tools to manage safe-haven flows.

Long-term fiscal pressures: Public debt reaches 39.4 percent of GDP in 2026. Demographics and climate could add 56 percent of GDP to debt by 2060. Staff advise revenue measures including VAT increases; authorities commit to debt-brake compliance.
